rules.explanation: Benzoyl peroxide is an oxidizer that can break down retinoids, and the combination is also very drying and irritating.
rules.suggestion: Use benzoyl peroxide in the morning and the retinoid at night, or on alternate nights.

rules.explanation: Benzoyl Peroxide oxidizes Vitamin C, reducing its efficacy.
rules.suggestion: Move Vitamin C to night or alternate days.

rules.explanation: Both increase cell turnover. Layering them raises the risk of redness, peeling, and a damaged barrier.
Both can dry and irritate the skin when used together, especially if you are new to either.
rules.suggestion: Alternate nights, and introduce one at a time.

rules.explanation: Both are potent actives that work best at different pH levels and can sting when layered.
rules.suggestion: Vitamin C in the morning, retinoid at night.

rules.explanation: Both can cause dryness or stinging, particularly while your skin is adjusting.
rules.suggestion: Introduce slowly, or use at different times of day.

rules.explanation: Stacking two low-pH actives can sting and over-exfoliate sensitive skin.
rules.suggestion: Use vitamin C in the morning and the AHA at night.

rules.explanation: Stacking two low-pH actives can sting, especially on dry or reactive skin.
rules.suggestion: Use at different times of day.

rules.explanation: Using two exfoliating acids together can over-exfoliate and weaken your skin barrier.
Both are strong and drying. Together they can leave skin tight, red, or flaky.
rules.suggestion: Use on different days or at different times of day.

rules.explanation: Both target breakouts and can be very drying when combined.
rules.suggestion: Start with one, and add the other slowly or on alternate days.

rules.explanation: Both can dry the skin. They are often used together, but watch for tightness or stinging.
rules.suggestion: Patch test first and introduce slowly.

rules.explanation: Niacinamide supports your barrier while hyaluronic acid draws in water, so hydration lasts longer.
Niacinamide can help soften retinoid dryness and irritation, so the pair is often better tolerated.
Hyaluronic acid adds hydration that offsets the dryness retinoids can cause.
Vitamin C adds antioxidant protection under sunscreen, helping defend against environmental damage.
Retinoids make skin more sun-sensitive. Daily SPF protects your results and your skin.
They work well together. Niacinamide supports the barrier while vitamin C targets dullness and dark spots.
Hyaluronic acid hydrates and ceramides seal that moisture in.
Both soothe and support a stressed barrier, so they reinforce each other.
Hyaluronic acid hydrates while peptides support firmness, so they complement each other.
Peptides are gentle and can support skin while a retinoid does the heavy lifting.
